media.alt: Hepatits A to E and liver cancer

content.text: "Diagnosis of acute viral Hepatitis is established by blood tests and are presented in two modes, i.e. Jaundice and Non-Jaundice. Out of five serologically distinguishable types - Hepatitis B, C and 0 may culminates in chronic types", informed Dr Wasim Jafri, Consultant Gastroentrologist and Associate Professor of Medicine, The Aga Khan University Hospital, Karachi. He was giving a presentation on "Hepatitis A to E and Liver Cancer" at 'Signs, Symptoms and Care', monthly health awareness program, held on December 18, 1999.

Dr Jafri added,"In the past 20 to 30 years, Hepatitis C produce chronically in more than 70 percent- 90 percent of the cases and chronic liver disease (Cirrhosis) develops in 20 percent-30 percent of patients. Bad hygiene, infected water and food transmit types A and E whereas types B, C, and 0 are mainly through blood, blood products and sexual contacts. The source of infection is unknown in one third of Hepatitis B and one half of Hepatitis C."
Dr Jafri concluded by saying that Hepatitis Band C could result in chronic Liver disease and Liver Cancer. Active and passive prophylaxis is available for Hepatitis A and B only."
